# Meet Diego

Diego Licona (he/him) is a dual Master of Public Health (MPH) and Master of Public Administration (MPA) Candidate at Columbia University's Mailman School of Public Health (MSPH) and School of Interantional and Public Affairs (SIPA). He holds a Bachelor's degree from New York University (NYU), where he majored in Chemistry and Social & Cultural Analysis. His academic training has focused on understanding health across multiple levels——from molecular mechanisms of disease to the social and structural forces that shape health outcomes——leading him to pursue an MPH/MPA to integrate clinical science, data science, and public health advocacy.

Before joining SIPA, Diego had co-led community-based health projects in Mexico and Zambia through local and international agencies such as UNHCR, the Eastern Mediterranean Public Health Network, and most recently with NYC's Preparedness and Response Institute. Diego's work is deeply influenced by the diverse refugee communities in his hometown, Tijuana, at the US-Mexico border, where he participated in clinical initiatives providing health care services to asylum-seeking individuals. Given his experience in street medicine, LGBTQ+ care, and peer-to-peer health education, he has served as a patient advocate, clinical volunteer, and full-time research coordinator for health systems in NYC. He strives to improve healthcare outcomes for migrant and forcibly displaced populations through research, data, and policy.

During his free time, Diego enjoys time outdoors, discovering new coffee shops, reading, and writing. Feel free to connect with him on LinkedIn or via email!
